He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class. ==Early life and high school career== Dylan Harper grew up in [[Franklin Lakes, New Jersey]] and attended [[Don Bosco Preparatory High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2023/01/11/dylan-harper-top-nj-basketball-recruit-don-bosco/69766435007/|title=Considered a top HS basketball talent in NJ, Dylan Harper does it all on and off the court|work=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]|first=Greg|last=Mattura|date=January 11, 2023|access-date=March 2, 2023}} He averaged 15.2 points per game during his sophomore season.{{cite web|url=https://indiana.rivals.com/news/indiana-extends-offer-to-top-50-2024-guard-dylan-harper|title=Indiana extends offer to top-50 2024 guard Dylan Harper|first=Alec|last=Lasley|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 25, 2023|access-date=July 19, 2023}} Harper was named the Boys Basketball Player of the Year by ''[[NJ.com]]'' as a junior after averaging 24.9 points, six rebounds, three assists, and two steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Yc3gUeKu3USlr-fe-ECyyg/high-school-basketball-could-dylan-harper-have-a-better-nba-career-than-his-father-ron-harper.htm|title=High school basketball: Could Dylan Harper have a better NBA career than his father Ron Harper?|first=Jordan|last=Divens|website=[[MaxPreps]]|date=May 24, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2023/03/don-bosco-preps-dylan-harper-is-the-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-2022-23.html|title=Don Bosco Prep’s Dylan Harper is the Boys Basketball Player of the Year, 2022-23|first=Brandon|last=Gould|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=March 20, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} Harper averaged 22.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game while leading the Ironmen to a 29–3 record and a NJSIAA Non-Public A state championship during his senior season. Harper played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball for the New York Renaissance.{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2022/07/nj-star-dylan-harper-leads-ny-rens-into-peach-jam-semis-says-rutgers-is-recruiting-him-the-hardest.html|title=N.J. star Dylan Harper leads NY Rens into Peach Jam semis, says Rutgers is recruiting him the hardest|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=July 22, 2022|access-date=March 2, 2023}} ===Recruiting=== Harper was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2023/07/at-nike-peach-jam-rutgers-remains-laser-focused-on-no-1-target-dylan-harper.html|title=At Nike Peach Jam, Rutgers remains laser-focused on No. 1 target Dylan Harper|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=July 7, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} He was rated the number one overall recruit for the class of 2024 by ''[[ESPN]]'' during the summer before the start of his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/insider/story/_/id/37905743/men-college-basketball-recruiting-updated-rankings-no-1-risers-new-faces|title=Rising men's college basketball recruits, a new No. 1, more|first=Paul|last=Biancardi|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=June 28, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} On December 6, 2023, Harper committed to playing college basketball for [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], his brother‘s alma mater, over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Indiana
